# Nodara

> Experimental bounded RPC for Node.js microservices, with a Rust broker and a multi-broker TypeScript client. Formerly VeloBus. MIT licensed.

The npm package is `nodara` (Node.js 20+, ESM/CommonJS). Brokers run separately.
Multi-broker mode balances new calls and restores registrations after reconnect;
it does not replicate queues or replay uncertain operations. Use durable business
idempotency and reconciliation when handling payments or orders.

## Integration

- [Full agent guide](https://github.com/AssisCabron/VeloBus/blob/main/LLM.txt): API examples, defaults, capacity accounting and failure semantics.
- [Client README](https://github.com/AssisCabron/VeloBus/blob/main/packages/client/README.md): npm installation and worker/caller examples.
- [Multiple brokers](https://github.com/AssisCabron/VeloBus/blob/main/docs/CLUSTER.md): balancing, reconnect, shared worker concurrency and limitations.

## Protocol and evidence

- [RPC protocol](https://github.com/AssisCabron/VeloBus/blob/main/docs/RPC-PROTOCOL.md): binary request/reply extension and error codes.
- [Event protocol](https://github.com/AssisCabron/VeloBus/blob/main/docs/PROTOCOL.md): node-local event history and WAL.
- [Historical benchmarks](https://github.com/AssisCabron/VeloBus/blob/main/docs/RPC-BENCHMARKS.md): single-broker v0.2 measurements; not a cluster/Pi benchmark.
